reasoning_traces.think:
The axial transformer framework models football dynamics through a structured agent-time grid where each cell encodes a player or team's state at a given game moment. Temporal attention enforces causality by allowing only past information to influence future predictions, while agent attention captures interdependencies among players and teams. This dual attention mechanism enables joint modeling of match outcomes, team totals, and individual player actions. The Poisson-NLL loss function aligns with the discrete nature of football actions such as receptions, rushes, and touchdowns, ensuring that forecasts reflect realistic variability. Training uses Adam optimizer with cosine decay, achieving sub-second inference on commodity hardware. The model's design supports scalable deployment in GSE for real-time forecasting.
